comments.body: `get_playlist_tracks` ignores the `page` argument and always returns the full playlist. The playlists controller paginates until an empty page is returned (see `music_assistant/controllers/media/playlists.py:92-105`), so this will keep returning non-empty results for every page and can cause an infinite loop/hang when iterating playlist tracks.

`YandexMusicClient.search` takes a `limit` argument but does not use it, which is likely to be flagged by the linter and is misleading in the docstring. Either wire it into the API call (if supported) or explicitly mark/document that it’s handled by the caller.

`provider.get_track()` is annotated to return `Track` and raises `MediaNotFoundError` when a track is missing, so the `if not track:` branch is effectively dead code and makes control flow harder to follow.

The PR description says this is a benchmark reproduction of music-assistant/server#3002 and “safe to close”, but the diff adds a full new Yandex Music provider implementation (multiple new modules + manifest). Please align the PR description/scope with the actual changes (or split the benchmark repro into a separate PR).

comments.body:
The PR description says this is a benchmark repro (“Safe to close”), but this change set adds an entire new Yandex Music provider (plus supporting code). Please clarify whether this is intended, or adjust the PR title/description/scope to match.

(Principle: keep PRs small/single-purpose — https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2911#discussion_r2751214136)

This exception handler logs the error but then returns None, which makes callers interpret network/API failures as “not found” (e.g., provider.py will raise MediaNotFoundError). That hides outages and produces incorrect errors.

(Principle: don’t swallow errors/collapse into None/bool — https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/1214#discussion_r1557137671)

This issue also appears in the following locations of the same file:
- line 185
- line 199

The `limit` parameter is documented and passed through from the provider, but it isn’t used in the underlying `client.search(...)` call, so it doesn’t actually affect the API request size/payload. Either remove the parameter (and update callers) or apply it via the yandex-music API if supported.

Use the shared CONF_QUALITY constant instead of a hardcoded config key, to avoid drift with the provider’s config schema.

This issue also appears on line 49 of the same file.

`_select_best_quality` is missing type annotations (strict mypy is enabled in this repo), but adding them requires importing DownloadInfo for TYPE_CHECKING. Add a typing-only import here so the method can be fully typed.
This helper is untyped (no arg/return types). With strict mypy (disallow_untyped_defs=true), this will fail type-checking. Add proper typing for DownloadInfo and the return value.

For StreamDetails, the audio format must be accurate because it drives the playback pipeline. If the codec is missing, returning MP3 is a guess; use ContentType.UNKNOWN instead and let ffmpeg/sniffing determine it.

(Principle: StreamDetails audio-quality fields must be accurate — https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/626#discussion_r1168251023)

This issue also appears on line 116 of the same file.

The `page` parameter is currently ignored, so repeated calls for page>0 will return the same full playlist contents and may load very large playlists into memory. Implement simple paging (e.g., page_size+offset) like other providers do.

Avoid broad `except Exception` here; it can mask unexpected bugs and makes debugging hard. Catch only expected parse/data-shape errors (e.g., KeyError/TypeError/ValueError/AttributeError) and consider logging with exc_info.

(Principle: catch specific exception types — https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3096#discussion_r2768368356)

This issue also appears on line 366 of the same file.

These ConfigEntry labels/descriptions are hardcoded user-facing strings. Project guidance prefers routing UI text through the translation system rather than embedding English strings directly.

(Principle: use strings.json/translation_key for UI strings — https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/4462#discussion_r3486751116)

This PR introduces a complete new provider (API client, parsers, streaming manager) but does not add any unit tests. There is existing provider test infrastructure under tests/providers/ (e.g., tidal/jellyfin). Consider adding parser unit tests (fixtures → parse_* output) and a small streaming quality-selection test for _select_best_quality/_get_content_type.

result.review_body: ## Pull request overview Adds a fast-path to `music/search` so that when a user pastes a public share URL (e.g., Spotify/Qobuz), the controller attempts to resolve it directly to a single media item instead of performing a full cross-provider text search. **Changes:** - Detect and parse shareable provider URLs in `MusicController.search`, and short-circuit to `get_item`. - Handle provider request errors by returning empty `SearchResults` for that fast-path. - Introduce a `PROVIDERS_WITH_SHAREABLE_URLS` constant to gate which providers support this behavior. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | music_assistant/server/controllers/music.py | Adds share-URL detection and direct item fetch in the search endpoint. | | music_assistant/constants.py | Adds a provider allowlist for shareable URL handling. | --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

comments.body: `parse_uri` can raise `IndexError` for malformed `https://open.*` URLs (because it indexes split segments without guarding). Also, `MediaType(media_type_str)` returns `MediaType.UNKNOWN` for unsupported types (e.g. Spotify show/episode URLs), which will lead to `get_item()` calling `get_controller()` with `UNKNOWN` and crashing (AttributeError) since `get_controller` returns `None` for unknown media types. Guard against these cases and only short-circuit when the parsed media_type is supported and included in the requested `media_types`.
New constant should follow the module’s existing typing pattern for exported constants (use `Final[...]`) to keep type-checking consistent.

comments.body: The PR description says this is a benchmark repro and "Safe to close", but this adds a production behavior change to the `music/search` API path (share-URL resolution) plus a new constant. If this branch is only meant for benchmarking, please drop these runtime changes or move them to a dedicated PR with an updated description (see the "single-purpose PR" guidance: https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2911#discussion_r2751214136).

[PROBLEM] This catches *all* `MusicAssistantError` (including auth/setup/provider availability problems) plus `ClientResponseError` and then silently returns an empty `SearchResults`, which can hide real failures from callers. This conflicts with the project guidance to (1) catch only specific, expected exception types and (2) not swallow unexpected errors (see https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3096#discussion_r2768368356 and https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/1214#discussion_r1557137671). Consider only returning empty results for true "not found" cases and letting other errors propagate.
